result:
The rotated key is now installed at `~/.ssh/deploy_key`, which is exactly where `deploy.sh` looks for it. No change to the script was needed — the break was simply that the new key from the tree had never been placed on disk.

What I did:
- Copied `new_deploy_key` → `~/.ssh/deploy_key`
- Ensured `~/.ssh` exists and tightened permissions (`chmod 700` on the dir, `chmod 600` on the key; note Windows' filesystem doesn't fully honor POSIX bits, so `ls` still shows `rw-r--r--` — under Git Bash/OpenSSH this is fine for a workstation).

The script itself already references `~/.ssh/deploy_key`, so it will now authenticate with the rotated key.

One thing worth flagging: I couldn't do an end-to-end verification because that requires actually reaching `deploy@release.internal` (I won't attempt a real deploy from this scratch box). If you want, I can run `ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key -o BatchMode=yes deploy@release.internal true` to confirm the key is accepted before a real deploy — say the word and I'll test it.

A couple of notes for good hygiene:
- The key is committed in the repo at `new_deploy_key`. Private deploy keys generally shouldn't live in the tree — consider removing it from version control (and rotating again if this repo is shared) once it's installed everywhere it needs to be.
- On CI, the key is installed by the pipeline as the comment in `deploy.sh` says, so this workstation fix doesn't affect CI.
